title: The 26,000 Year Clock

segments.text: How long does one full swing take?
Your axis is not just wobbling; it traces a shape like a double cone.
The half‑aperture is about 23.4 degrees, the obliquity of the ecliptic.
The rate is not constant; it’s about 25,772 years now but varies.
The motion is continuous, slow, and steady.
Your stars drift and seasons shift.
The answer lies in gravity pulling on Earth’s axis.

question: Did you think the clock’s speed was steady or variable?
